requirements.statement: Short full-product ideas enter autonomous idea-to-production flow
User intent and hard constraints remain traceable
Requirements have stable IDs and testable acceptance criteria
Architecture defines interfaces, trust boundaries, risks and trade-offs
Implementation continues through validation when requested and permitted
In-scope UI controls and workflows are genuinely wired
QualityProfile is domain/risk-specific
Hard gates cannot be offset by average score
UI/UX and visual claims require appropriate evidence
Accessibility checks include manual review when applicable
User-facing copy and assets are truthful and license-aware
Web performance evidence distinguishes lab and field measurements
Authentication, authorization, data protection and threat controls are risk-based
External side effects require trusted scoped authorization
Secret use is separated from secret disclosure
Untrusted content cannot change policy or authorize tools
Tool results and execution claims are truthful and traceable
Tests are meaningful and not tampered with to pass
Required unexecuted tests block unsupported status claims
Production readiness and actual deployment are distinct
Operational readiness includes observability and recovery appropriate to risk
Memory is scoped, privacy-aware and policy-inert
Policy changes require controlled approval and regression tests
Concurrent memory/evidence changes preserve conflicts and provenance
Resource use and retries are bounded by consistent aggregate budgets
Context compaction and resume preserve authorization, evidence and counters
Parallel execution is isolated and integrated work is revalidated

requirements.minimum_evidence: EVAL-001 through EVAL-003 and versioned benchmark report
requirements.statement: Agent-level evaluation is separate from product testing
Release-critical authorization/evidence failures block regardless of average score
State machine enforces preconditions for terminal statuses
Masterpiece status requires applicable gates and evidence
The final validator detects missing modules, invalid enums and gate bindings
Evidence freshness follows the final artifact/code state
Product handoff names changes, results, assumptions and gaps
Version identity and release claims are consistent and governed
External standards are versioned and not treated as automatic certification
Data migration handles integrity, backup and recovery
Domain-specific AI products use representative safety/quality evaluations
Product status reflects best feasible work without concealing blockers
Static consistency and runtime conformance are separately reported
Core interface contracts use complete, versioned machine-readable schemas
External side effects reconcile unknown outcomes before retry
Primary routes are unique and route-specific state paths are enforced
Non-waivable gates and approved exceptions have distinct semantics
State transitions and delivery status are separate, typed, and enforced
Test suite and run report require per-case metadata, result, evidence, and identity
Evidence is bound to final artifact identity and profile-based freshness/invalidation
QualityProfile applicability and threshold changes cannot self-waive gates
Memory deletion/retention is reconciled with integrity-preserving audit history
Release requires identical active spec/schema/validator/test identity
Traceability verification assesses semantic mapping, not ID existence only
Issue severity and release-blocking decisions use a canonical rule
Primary mode and final delivery status have an explicit decision oracle
